headline: Messi's next move: Lionel Messi acquires Spanish clubs for post-retirement plan
summary: The football legend is building a multi-country football empire focusing on youth development, including the acquisition of CD Eldense and UE Cornella.
details: Lionel Messi is preparing for life after football by investing in club ownership. The 39-year-old has recently completed the acquisition of Spanish second-tier club CD Eldense, adding it to his portfolio alongside UE Cornella, a Catalan fifth-tier side he bought in April.

According to BBC Sport, Messi's strategy involves using UE Cornella as a breeding ground for young talent, while CD Eldense serves as the primary operation. He is not yet managing the day-to-day operations, using trusted associates to link him to the Spanish sides.

Messi has expressed a lack of interest in coaching, stating he wants to own clubs and help children develop their skills. He has also partnered with Luis Suarez in Uruguay's Deportivo LSM, a project focused on youth development that won promotion to the third tier in its first season.

Beyond club ownership, Messi's Inter Miami contract includes a future stake in the MLS club after he retires. He is also expanding the Messi Cup, an under-16 tournament in Miami, which has doubled its field to 16 academies, including giants like Barcelona and Manchester City.

The football star has diversified his investments into hotels, property, and restaurants. Despite his global fame, Messi has admitted to the America Business Forum that he is still learning the fundamentals of business management.
caption:

Lionel Messi is preparing for life after football by investing in club ownership. The 39-year-old has recently completed the acquisition of Spanish second-tier club CD Eldense, adding it to his portfolio alongside UE Cornella, a Catalan fifth-tier side he bought in April.

According to BBC Sport, Messi's strategy involves using UE Cornella as a breeding ground for young talent, while CD Eldense serves as the primary operation. He is not yet managing the day-to-day operations, using trusted associates to link him to the Spanish sides.

Messi has expressed a lack of interest in coaching, stating he wants to own clubs and help children develop their skills. He has also partnered with Luis Suarez in Uruguay's Deportivo LSM, a project focused on youth development that won promotion to the third tier in its first season.

Beyond club ownership, Messi's Inter Miami contract includes a future stake in the MLS club after he retires. He is also expanding the Messi Cup, an under-16 tournament in Miami, which has doubled its field to 16 academies, including giants like Barcelona and Manchester City.

The football star has diversified his investments into hotels, property, and restaurants. Despite his global fame, Messi has admitted to the America Business Forum that he is still learning the fundamentals of business management.

headline: Ronaldo accuses coach Jorge Jesus of breaking promises in explosive statement
summary: The Portugal captain claims he left the national team camp after the coach failed to honor agreements regarding his playing time and public clarification.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo has accused Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of twice breaking his word, leading to his sudden departure from the training camp in Copenhagen.

The 41-year-old forward stated that he and Jesus had agreed on a plan to manage his fitness by missing the Norway and Denmark matches, but the coach later changed the plan on the day of the Norway game.
Ronaldo claims that despite warming up from halftime onwards, he was never called on to play, which he described as a mistake by the coach.
The dispute escalated when Ronaldo says Jesus failed to honor an agreement to publicly clarify the events at a press conference, despite an eight-point document being prepared.
Ronaldo stated that the coach's public remarks did not resemble their private discussions, prompting him to leave the camp without waiting for further broken promises.
Coach Jorge Jesus has denied making any such agreement with the player, though he has left the door open for Ronaldo's return to the squad.
Ronaldo apologized for failing to greet supporters and leaving his teammates, acknowledging that his role as captain makes his conduct more serious.

The forward has called for the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) to assess and punish his actions, while insisting he remains available to compete for the national team once any suspension is served.
caption:
Cristiano Ronaldo claims he was betrayed by his own coach. Why did the football legend leave the Portugal camp?

Cristiano Ronaldo has accused Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of twice breaking his word, leading to his sudden departure from the training camp in Copenhagen.

The 41-year-old forward stated that he and Jesus had agreed on a plan to manage his fitness by missing the Norway and Denmark matches, but the coach later changed the plan on the day of the Norway game.

Ronaldo claims that despite warming up from halftime onwards, he was never called on to play, which he described as a mistake by the coach.

The dispute escalated when Ronaldo says Jesus failed to honor an agreement to publicly clarify the events at a press conference, despite an eight-point document being prepared.

Ronaldo stated that the coach's public remarks did not resemble their private discussions, prompting him to leave the camp without waiting for further broken promises.

Coach Jorge Jesus has denied making any such agreement with the player, though he has left the door open for Ronaldo's return to the squad.

Ronaldo apologized for failing to greet supporters and leaving his teammates, acknowledging that his role as captain makes his conduct more serious.

The forward has called for the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) to assess and punish his actions, while insisting he remains available to compete for the national team once any suspension is served.
